identity: DARK-NUMBER window: for floors in (theta*, f_D) the population crosses the critical line yet the escape excess is below 3 sigma at n=64000 - catastrophe without statistics.  The boundary's shadow: near-critical populations can be in trouble silently.

windows.dark_regime: f < theta*: no excess escapes (0.20 plateau exact), safe and blind
windows.silent_crossing: (theta* = 0.06332, f_D = 0.06867), width (f_D-theta*)/theta* = 0.0846: excess exists, < 3 sigma, unreadable
windows.twilight: (f_D, f_S = 0.070): audible but naive reading still biased (|z_book|>1)
windows.luminous: f >= f_S: the threshold reads within 1 sigma
windows.ethics: in the silent window the naive observer sees the plateau and cannot distinguish theta* from f_D - metamery.  Design: either stay strictly below the line (accept blindness) or cross it LOUDLY (f >= f_D, and better f >= f_S).  Operating in (theta*, f_D) buys events without knowledge.

scaling.rule: SE_p ~ 1/sqrt(n), so f_D descends toward theta* and the silent window SHRINKS: darkness is a finite-sample phenomenon.

design_number: loud crossing at n=64000 requires floor f >= 0.0700 (10.6% above theta*); 3-sigma audibility at f_D = 0.0687.
references_note: binomial power analysis for the 3-sigma audibility threshold (Cohen 1988, Statistical Power Analysis; Casella & Berger 2002, Statistical Inference); survival/quants after Barlow & Proschan 1975; the boundary's use as the NSE-live assignment unchanged.
